description: An assistant principal must approve a student's re-entry plan after a short suspension, including the student's return schedule, transition support, counseling check-ins, and restorative meeting arrangements, with input from the student's teacher and school counselor.

shared_context.S1: An eighth-grade student is scheduled to return next Monday after a three-day suspension for a hallway altercation.
shared_context.S2: Ms. Grant approves the student's binding re-entry and behavior-support plan.
shared_context.S3: The current draft returns the student to the regular schedule, includes a weekly counselor check-in, and schedules a restorative conference after school during the first week back.
shared_context.S4: The school normally reviews a re-entry plan with the student's teacher and counselor before it is finalized.

PF1.text: Mr. Bell observed that the student's altercations occur during crowded passing periods and that the student has a documented conflict with the peer assigned as the draft's peer mentor; he recorded these observations in his classroom notebook this week, but they have not yet been entered into the behavior-support system.

PF2.text: Ms. Ortiz reviewed the student's counseling file and confirmed with the guardian yesterday that the student must provide evening care for a younger sibling, so an after-school conference is not possible; the student also needs daily counselor check-ins for the first 10 school days because recent counseling notes show escalating anxiety around returning to school, but neither update is in the re-entry draft yet.

acceptance_conditions: The student must begin with a staggered return schedule.
The student must receive adult-escorted transition support for exactly 10 school days.
The peer mentor arrangement must be canceled.
The student must receive daily counselor check-ins for exactly 10 school days.
The restorative meeting must occur during the school day.
A formal re-entry behavior-plan documentation commitment must be recorded.
A family-schedule coordination commitment must be recorded.

decisive_facts.why: The passing-period observations require changing the regular return to a staggered return, setting adult-escorted transition support at exactly 10 school days, and removing the peer mentor assignment.

The counselor's confirmed family-care constraint moves the restorative meeting into the school day, while the anxiety finding changes check-ins from weekly to daily for exactly 10 school days and requires family-schedule coordination.
